title: parse.rs preview double-limits: decode max_bytes=256, then chars().take(256)
description: parse.rs lines 43-49: decode_body_value is called with max_bytes=Some(256) (byte limit), then .chars().take(256) is applied to the result. For multibyte UTF-8 (e.g. Chinese text), 256 bytes decode to fewer than 256 chars, so the preview is further truncated to fewer than 256 chars. For ASCII, 256 bytes == 256 chars, which is fine. But for single-byte encodings like ISO-8859-1 that require 2 UTF-8 bytes per char (e.g. extended Latin), 256 decoded bytes encode to up to 512 UTF-8 bytes, and .take(256) then cuts the preview at 256 *characters* not *source bytes*. The intent (256-char preview) is correct but the byte limit and char limit are redundant; the byte limit may truncate mid-character and is_encoding_problem is then set unnecessarily.
